summary: The design fits the existing BasicAuth session boundary, but several lifecycle and security contracts are underspecified. The largest risks are tenant-policy resolution, pre-session vault access, fail-open infrastructure, and an undefined second-step login protocol.

suggestions.title: Resolve MFA policy per request, not at backend startup
suggestions.rationale: Backends are process-lifetime objects initialized once in AuthHandler.auth_startup(), while tenant policy is mutable data. Load policy using the authenticated user’s canonical tenant membership after password validation; do not use request headers or a startup snapshot as the source of truth.

suggestions.title: Define an explicit non-session MFA challenge contract
suggestions.rationale: api_login() treats any truthy backend result as a completed login and immediately calls load_session(); BasicAuth.authenticate() currently calls open_session() directly. Add a distinct challenge response/exception and a second verification route or request mode, with the challenge bound to user, tenant, first-factor event, expiry, and single-use consumption.

suggestions.title: Make every MFA dependency fail closed
suggestions.rationale: RateLimiter.check() explicitly returns allowed on Redis errors, and the existing vault startup/load integration logs failures and continues. A copied limiter or vault call can silently bypass MFA unless verification storage, policy reads, seed reads, and replay checks use a separate fail-closed path.

suggestions.title: Do not use the session-scoped vault API before a session exists
suggestions.rationale: MFA verification occurs before open_session(), but load_vault_for_session() requires a session_id and get_session_vault() loads/caches against an existing session. Add a narrowly scoped pre-session user-secret operation or a factor repository that uses the vault crypto primitives without fabricating a session.

suggestions.title: Treat MFA schema initialization as a required migration
suggestions.rationale: Auth startup invokes backend initialization before vault setup, while setup_vault_tables() catches DDL failures and continues. For an enabled tenant policy, missing or partially applied factor tables must prevent MFA-enabled startup or make all affected logins reject; use an ordered, observable migration with concurrency protection.

suggestions.title: Protect tenant lookup from header and global-default confusion
suggestions.rationale: _resolve_tenant() gives trusted headers and explicit arguments priority over userinfo, then falls back to (1,1). Reusing it for login enforcement can apply one tenant’s policy to another or silently select the global policy. MFA lookup should use the canonical user record or a validated membership pair and reject ambiguity.

suggestions.title: Specify factor-state transitions independently from passkey credentials
suggestions.rationale: PasskeyAuth stores credentials in user_credentials and only guards deletion against other login methods; it has no shared MFA-state record. The proposed none/email/totp transitions therefore cannot consistently close or reopen email fallback when TOTP or passkeys are enrolled, removed, or revoked.

suggestions.title: Require reauthentication and explicit authorization for factor management
suggestions.rationale: user_session() only attaches the existing session user, and the default admin policies authorize by group without an MFA condition. Enrollment, disenrollment, policy changes, and trusted-device revocation need dedicated routes with current-password or recent-MFA proof, ABAC actions, tenant ownership checks, and protection against self-lockout.

suggestions.title: Do not treat existing UserDevices as trusted MFA devices
suggestions.rationale: UserDevices contains long-lived API/JWT credentials and a revoked flag, not browser trust state. Reusing it would conflate bearer API credentials with a second-factor bypass. Either remove trusted devices from this scope or define separate hashed opaque tokens, expiry/rotation, policy binding, and revocation semantics.

suggestions.title: Make security-transition audit records durable and action-specific
suggestions.rationale: Existing guard auditing and AuditLog writes are explicitly best-effort and represent authorization decisions, not factor state changes. Persist actor, target user, tenant, old/new state, method, request identity, and outcome through a durable audit row or outbox for enrollment, disenrollment, policy changes, and revocation.

suggestions.title: Test invariants at the session boundary and under races
suggestions.rationale: Tests should prove no provider or challenge endpoint can call remember/create_token, password-only requests never mint a session when policy requires MFA, TokenExchangeAuth and PasskeyAuth remain unaffected, Redis/vault/DB failures reject verification, concurrent code submissions consume once, TOTP steps cannot replay, and tenant A cannot use tenant B’s policy or factor.
